questions.question: Which pair of properties is required to create a gradient text effect in CSS?
questions.hint: Background clipped to text with transparent fill.
questions.explanation: -webkit-background-clip: text clips the gradient background to the text shape, while -webkit-text-fill-color: transparent allows the background to shine through.

questions.question: Which layout tool is optimal for building a two-column desktop layout with a 280px sidebar and a fluid main content area?
questions.explanation: grid-template-columns: 280px 1fr elegantly creates a fixed 280px sidebar alongside a fluid remaining fraction (1fr).

questions.question: How do you ensure a sticky sidebar stops scrolling when it reaches the bottom of its parent container?
options: position: sticky with top: 24px inside a defined parent container
questions.hint: position: sticky stays constrained within its parent boundary.
questions.explanation: position: sticky naturally respects parent container boundaries, automatically unsticking when the parent scrolls out of view.

questions.question: Why should buttons wrapped in a button group use flex-wrap: wrap?
options: To make buttons spin on click
To prevent buttons from overflowing and clipping on narrow smartphone screens
questions.hint: Allows buttons to wrap to a new line on small screens.
questions.explanation: flex-wrap: wrap allows multiple buttons to stack neatly onto subsequent lines on small mobile screens.

questions.question: What is the recommended rule of thumb for choosing between CSS Grid and Flexbox in web applications?
options: Use Grid for everything, never use Flexbox
Use Grid for 2D macro-layouts and card matrices; use Flexbox for 1D micro-components and alignment
Use Flexbox for images and Grid for text
questions.hint: Grid for 2D page architecture; Flexbox for 1D component flow.
questions.explanation: Grid excels at 2-dimensional page layouts and card grids, while Flexbox is ideal for 1-dimensional navigation, toolbars, and content alignment.
